paper_title: Can We Edit LLMs for Long-Tail Biomedical Knowledge
caption_used: The performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, where "Base" denotes LLM without editing. The x-axis shows co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale, while the y-axis represents accuracy (ACC %). All six methods show improving accuracy with increasing co-occurrence frequency. ROME consistently achieves the highest accuracy, starting at approximately 51% and reaching roughly 66% at the highest co-occurrence numbers. MEND and MEMIT follow as the next best performers, with MEND reaching approximately 56% and MEMIT approximately 55%. Notably, IKE demonstrates a steeper improvement rate than FT, surpassing it at co-occurrence numbers above 10^2 to reach approximately 52% at the highest frequency. The Base model exhibits the lowest performance throughout, plateauing at approximately 44%.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC %) as a function of the Co-occurrence Number for six different methods: Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME. The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" and uses a logarithmic scale with visible major tick labels at 0, $10^{1}$, $10^{2}$, and $10^{3}$. The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)", plotted on a linear scale, with visible tick marks ranging from 40 to 65 at regular increments of 5. The plot features six solid lines evaluated across four distinct data points along the x-axis. The Base method is represented by a black line with circular markers; it begins at an accuracy of approximately 38%, increases to roughly 44% at the third data point, and levels off near 44% at the final data point. The FT method is shown as a blue line with downward-pointing triangle markers, steadily increasing from roughly 40% at the start to approximately 48% at the end. The IKE method is plotted with a red line and upward-pointing triangle markers, showing a steady rise from approximately 43% initially to roughly 49% at the final point. The MEND method features a brown line with diamond markers, starting at about 44% and climbing to approximately 56% at the highest co-occurrence number. The MEMIT method is depicted by a purple line with pentagon markers, rising from roughly 43.5% at the first x-value to approximately 55% at the last recorded x-value. Lastly, the ROME method is represented by a green line with square markers, starting at approximately 51% and increasing continuously to end at roughly 66%.
